AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 1, 2020
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
VIDEOCONFERENCED WITHOUT PROVIDING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR CALL (669) 900-
6833; MEETING ID: 890 5283 0731; PASSCODE: 568111 DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM
OR UNDER ORAL COMMUNICATIONS. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR
CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393 .
  6:30 PM
  VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a):
  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles
  County Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: APN 8056-017-901; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the
  City and Penny Reeves, Norwalk Auto Auction; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(2) in
  one case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  John Ramirez
  Director of Community Development

FLAG SALUTE
  Richard Rojas
  Deputy City Manager

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS None.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Recap of Paint the Town Pink Campaign.

  3.  Thanksgiving Basket Program and Luncheon recap.

  4.  Introduction of City’s new motor deputy.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  November 17 and 23, 2020. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period October 18, 2020 –
  October 31, 2020, in the total amount of $926,478.57. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  November 11, 2020 – November 24, 2020, in the total amount of $3,772,001.10. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  RESOLUTION NO. 20-77 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 20-77, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT AND PUBLIC SAFETY DEPARTMENTS. 870-02

  Report

  5.  PROJECT NO. 7521 – ACCEPTANCE OF WORK FOR THE SEWER SYSTEM REHABILITATION –
  PHASE 3 - Staff recommends City Council accept the construction work of Vasilj, Inc. in the amount of
  $1,170,344.86. 1005-04-7521

  Report

  6.  AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO ACCESS AGREEMENT – HOLIFIELD PARK - Staff recommends City Council
  approve Amendment No. 2 to the Access Agreement with the Source Group, Inc. for the installation of
  monitoring wells and continue their monitoring activities, as required by the California Regional Water
  Quality Control Board, at Holifield Park; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and
  any amendments on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 920-03-04

  Report

  7.  TRANSFER AGREEMENT - MEASURE W – CLEAN WATER PROGRAM – Staff recommends City
  Council approve the Transfer agreement with the Los Angeles Flood Control District - Safe Clean
  Water Program (SCWP) for Municipal Program Funds; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  Transfer Agreement and any amendments, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney. 1070

  Report

  8.  APPOINTMENT OF TRUSTEE – GREATER LOS ANGELES COUNTY VECTOR CONTROL
  DISTRICT - Staff recommends City Council confirm the Mayor’s nomination to appoint Councilmember
  Valencia to serve as a trustee on the Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District for a two-year
  term ending January 1, 2023. 825-09

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NO. 20-78 – AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO ACCESS STATE AND FEDERAL LEVEL
  SUMMARY CRIMINAL HISTORY INFORMATION FOR LICENSING PURPOSES - Staff recommends
  City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-78, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO ACCESS STATE AND FEDERAL LEVEL SUMMARY
  CRIMINAL HISTORY INFORMATION FOR LICENSING PURPOSES. 135-14

  Report

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 20-79 – AMEND 2020/21 SALARY SCHEDULE INCORPORATING THE
  CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE INCREASE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2021 - Staff recommends City
   Council adopt Resolution No. 20-79, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 FOR GENERAL AND
  HOURLY UNIT EMPLOYEES AND EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT UNIT
  EMPLOYEES TO INCORPORATE 2021 CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE REQUIREMENTS. 135-03

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 20-81 – AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER OR DESIGNEE TO APPLY FOR
  PROPOSITION 68 ALLOCATED GRANT FUNDS - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution
  No. 20-81, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING
  SUBMITTAL OF APPLICATIONS FOR PER CAPITA PROPOSITION 68 GRANT FUNDS. 623

  Report

  12. AGREEMENTS TO PROVIDE ON-CALL BUILDING & SAFETY AND PLANNING CONSULTING
  SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve agreements with the seven (7) selected firms
  listed above to provide on-call planning and/or on-call building and safety related services for a term of
  three (3) years from the date of execution, in an amount not to exceed $150,000 annually for each firm;
  and authorize the City Manager to execute agreements and any amendments provided there is funding
  in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 300

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  13. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 20-80 – ADOPTING ASSOCIATED FEES RELATED TO DIRECTOR APPROVAL
  PROCESS - ORDINANCE NO. 20-1720 - ADOPTING TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 320 AMENDING
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE (NMC) TITLE 5 AS IT RELATES TO SPECIAL EVENTS AND
  PAWNBROKERS AND TITLE 17 AS IT RELATES TO DEFINITIONS, APPROVAL PROCEDURES,
  SPECIFIC USE REQUIREMENTS, OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING REQUIREMENTS, SIGN
  STANDARDS, AND PERMITTED LAND USES, IN ORDER TO SUPPORT ECONOMIC
  DEVELOPMENT AND RECOVERY THROUGHOUT THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 20-80, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AMENDING THE COMPREHENSIVE FEE SCHEDULE TO ESTABLISH A FEE FOR
  DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST PROCESS in the amount of $1,500; and

  b.  introduce for first reading by title only Ordinance No. 20-1720, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AMENDING TITLE 5 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE AS IT RELATES TO
  SPECIAL EVENTS AND PAWNBROKERS AND TITLE 17 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE
  AS IT RELATES TO DEFINITIONS, APPROVAL PROCEDURES, SPECIFIC USE
  REQUIREMENTS, OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING REQUIREMENTS, SIGN
  STANDARDS, AND PERMITTED LAND USES AND FINDING THE ORDINANCE EXEMPT FROM
  THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT, and waive further reading. 602-01/320-05-
  320

  Report

REPORTS

  15. JANUARY MEETING SCHEDULE CONSIDERATION – Staff recommends City Council either:

  a.  direct staff to take the appropriate steps to move the meetings to January 12 and 26, 2021; or

  b.  cancel the January 5, 2021 meeting and authorize holding one regularly scheduled meeting on
  January 19, 2021. 825
   Report

  16. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – DECEMBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated November 25, 2020.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
